newsitem.title: GERMANY: VIAG optimistic of higher earnings in 1997.
newsitem.headline: VIAG optimistic of higher earnings in 1997.

text.p: Group net profit at the German diversified utility giant Viag AG fell in 1996, but the group said it was optimistic that it could raise earnings slightly in the current year.
Earnings in the first quarter were a cause for optimism, the group said, despite unavoidable, and well-signalled, losses in its telecommunications business.

In the first three months of the year, pre-tax profits grew to 674 million marks ($396 million) from 668 million marks, while group sales grew to 12.3 billion marks from 10.9 billion marks in the same quarter last year -- falling somewhat short of analysts' expectations.
Viag shares were quoted at 771 marks in pre-bourse trade, down 8.50 marks.
Group net profit for 1996 fell to 1.06 billion marks from 1.32 billion marks in 1995, while group sales grew to 12.3 billion marks from 10.9 billion marks in the same period.

"The fall in earnings can be attributed to clearly higher tax on earnings. Our tax charges were unusually low in 1995 because we could offset taxes against previous losses," the group said in a statement.

"For the current year we are optimistic that we can further increase our turnover and that we can maintain earnings at their current high level or even increase them slightly, despite unavoidable losses in telecommunications," Viag said.
The main contributors to growth in the first quarter were Viag's speciality chemical unit SKW Trostberg and its utility Bayernwerk, the group said.

It also said that on an adjusted basis, to account for the extraordinary earnings from the sale of the Didier unit included in last year's numbers, the group's profits would have climbed by seven percent.
Earnings per share (EPS), calculated using the DVFA German analysts' method, was 37.10 marks per share. This was close to market expectations.
According to the DVFA figures, contributions from its energy division, led by Bayernwerk, accounted for 77 percent of Viag's earnings.
Viag said seven percent came from chemicals, 16 percent from packaging and four percent from logistics.
